extra.message: Missing Authentication on All Sensitive Routes — Any anonymous attacker can access all data, execute OS commands, and perform all application actions without any credentials. [verified: No route in `do_GET` checks for a valid session cookie before serving data or executing actions; the `/login` route sets a session token but it is never validated on any subsequent request, leaving OS command execution, file read, pickle deserialization, and all other sensitive routes fully accessible to unauthenticated attackers.]

Insecure Deserialization (Pickle RCE) via ?object= parameter — Arbitrary code execution on the server; full host compromise. [verified: `pickle.loads(params['object'].encode())` deserializes attacker-controlled base64-encoded data with no validation; a malicious pickle payload with a `__reduce__` method can execute arbitrary OS commands upon deserialization.]

OS Command Injection via ?domain= parameter — Full OS command execution as the web server process user; can read any file, exfiltrate data, or establish a reverse shell. [verified: `subprocess.run('nslookup ' + params['domain'], shell=True, ...)` passes user-controlled input to a shell with `shell=True` and no sanitization, allowing full OS command injection via metacharacters like `;`, `&&`, or `|`.]

Path Traversal via ?include= Parameter (No Path Sanitization) — Attacker can read arbitrary files from the filesystem without the os.path.abspath() normalization present in the ?path= handler; file content is also executed via exec(), enabling RCE from any readable Python file on the system [verified: At line 56, when `://` is absent, `open(params['include'], 'rb')` is called on the raw user-supplied string with no path normalization (unlike `?path=` which calls `os.path.abspath()`), allowing `../../../etc/shadow`-style traversal. The file content is then `exec()`'d, making arbitrary readable file access equivalent to RCE if any Python file is reachable.]

SSRF via ?include= Parameter — Attacker can make the server issue arbitrary HTTP/HTTPS/FTP requests to internal infrastructure, cloud metadata endpoints, or external attacker-controlled servers; combined with exec() this enables full RCE if the attacker serves Python code [verified: At line 56, when `://` is present in `params['include']`, `urllib.request.urlopen(params['include'])` is called with no scheme/host/port validation, enabling SSRF to arbitrary internal/external URLs. The fetched content is then immediately `exec()`'d, creating a direct SSRF→RCE chain with no intervening controls.]

Remote Code Execution via exec() on ?include= parameter — Full server-side code execution; complete host compromise. [verified: The `include` branch fetches arbitrary local files or remote URLs and passes the raw bytes to `exec(program, envs)` with no validation or sandboxing; an attacker pointing `?include=` at an attacker-controlled URL achieves full server-side Python code execution.]

SQL Injection in /login password parameter — Authentication bypass; attacker can log in as any user including admin without knowing credentials. [verified: In the `/login` path, `params.get('password','')` is concatenated directly into the SQL query with no sanitization; only `username` has a regex filter (`re.sub(r'[^\w]', '',...)`), so classic SQLi bypass payloads like `' OR '1'='1` work on the password field to authenticate as any user.]

DOM-Based XSS via URL fragment (#lang=) — Execute arbitrary JavaScript via crafted URL sent to victim; session hijacking, phishing. [verified: The inline JavaScript in `HTML_PREFIX` writes `decodeURIComponent(document.location.hash.substring(index + 5))` directly to the DOM via `document.write()` without any sanitization, enabling DOM-based XSS via a crafted `#lang=<script>...` URL fragment.]

Passwords Stored in Plaintext (No Hashing) — Any database read primitive (path traversal, SQL injection, source disclosure) yields cleartext user passwords directly; no offline cracking step required, enabling immediate account takeover [verified: At line 20, `cursor.executemany` inserts passwords from USERS_XML directly into the `users` table with no hashing or KDF, and the login handler at line 67 compares them as plaintext strings; any read primitive (SQL injection UNION SELECT, path traversal source disclosure) yields cleartext credentials with no offline cracking required.]

Reflected XSS via ?id= SQL Result Display — Attacker can inject arbitrary JavaScript into the page via UNION-based SQL injection in the ?id= parameter; enables session hijacking, credential theft, or DOM manipulation [verified: At line 31, SQL query results are rendered via `'%s' % value` with no `html.escape()` call; since the `?id=` parameter is also injectable (raw string concatenation into SQL), an attacker can use UNION injection to place `` directly into a table cell, achieving XSS without any intervening sanitization or CSP.]

SQL Injection via ?id= parameter — Full database read; attacker can exfiltrate all usernames and plaintext passwords via UNION or boolean/time-based blind injection. [verified: At line 33 (the `if 'id' in params` branch), `params['id']` is concatenated directly into the SQL query string with no parameterization, type-casting, or sanitization. No middleware or decorator validates this parameter before it reaches the cursor.execute call.]

Path Traversal / Arbitrary File Read via ?path= parameter — Read any file accessible to the web server process, including /etc/passwd, SSH keys, application source code, and credentials. [verified: `open(os.path.abspath(params['path']), 'rb')` is called with the raw user-supplied path when it does not contain `://`; `os.path.abspath()` resolves traversal sequences but does not restrict to any safe root directory, allowing `../../etc/passwd` or absolute paths to read arbitrary files.]

Server-Side Request Forgery via ?path= parameter — Probe internal network services, read cloud metadata, or access internal admin interfaces not exposed publicly. [verified: When `params['path']` contains `://`, `urllib.request.urlopen(params['path'])` is called with no scheme or host restriction, enabling SSRF to internal services, cloud metadata endpoints, or local files via `file://`.]

XML External Entity Injection via ?xml= parameter — Read arbitrary local files or trigger SSRF via XML entity resolution. [verified: `lxml.etree.XMLParser(load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, no_network=False)` explicitly enables all XXE features; user-supplied XML from `params['xml']` is parsed with these settings, allowing entity-based local file disclosure and SSRF.]

Denial of Service via unbounded memory allocation in ?size= parameter — Crash the web server process via memory exhaustion; complete availability loss. [verified: The `size` branch computes `'#' * int(params['size'])` repeated `int(params['size'])` times in a list comprehension, creating quadratic memory allocation; a value like `9999999` would exhaust memory and crash the server process with no input bound enforced.]

Stored SQL Injection via ?comment= parameter — Arbitrary SQL execution; can drop tables, exfiltrate data, or corrupt the database. [verified: At the `comment` branch, `params['comment']` is interpolated via `%s` string formatting directly into an INSERT statement with no escaping or parameterization. Any SQL metacharacters in the comment value are passed verbatim to SQLite.]

Stored XSS via ?comment= parameter — Persistent JavaScript execution in every visitor's browser; can be used for session hijacking, credential harvesting, or defacement. [verified: `params['comment']` is stored in the database without escaping and later retrieved and rendered directly into HTML table cells without `html.escape()`, allowing stored XSS payloads to persist and execute for every visitor who views comments.]

Reflected XSS via ?redir= HTML Attribute Injection — Attacker can break out of the meta tag attribute and inject arbitrary HTML/JavaScript, enabling session hijacking and credential theft without requiring a real redirect target [verified: At line 61, `params['redir']` is interpolated unescaped into `<meta http-equiv="refresh" content="0; url=%s"/>`, so a payload like `"><script>alert(document.cookie)</script>` closes the attribute and tag and injects arbitrary JavaScript; there is no HTML-attribute encoding or validation applied to this parameter.]

Hardcoded Credentials in Source Code — Anyone with source code access obtains all user credentials immediately; passwords may be reused on other systems. [verified: `USERS_XML` at line 10 hardcodes plaintext credentials for all users (admin:7en8aiDoh!, dricci:12345, etc.) directly in source code, and these are also stored in plaintext in the SQLite database at init time; source code access immediately yields all credentials.]

XPath Injection via ?name= parameter — Bypass user lookups, extract other users' passwords from the in-memory XML user store. [verified: `params['name']` is interpolated directly into the XPath expression `.//user[name/text()='%s']` with no escaping, allowing injection of XPath operators (e.g., `' or '1'='1`) to bypass filters and extract arbitrary data from the in-memory XML user store including passwords.]

Cross-Site Request Forgery on comment submission — Attacker can force authenticated or anonymous users to submit arbitrary comments by embedding a URL in any page the victim visits. [verified: The `?comment=` endpoint accepts GET requests that perform an INSERT without any CSRF token or SameSite cookie protection; any page can trigger the state-changing write by embedding a crafted URL (e.g., in an `` tag), as explicitly demonstrated in the CASES list.]

Open Redirect via ?redir= parameter — Phishing attacks; trick users into visiting malicious sites while appearing to originate from the legitimate application. [verified: `params['redir']` is placed directly into a meta refresh tag URL with no validation or allowlist check, enabling open redirect to arbitrary external sites useful for phishing.]

Weak/Insecure Session Token Generation and Cookie Handling — Session tokens are predictable; lack of HttpOnly allows JavaScript to steal tokens; lack of Secure flag allows transmission over HTTP. [verified: The session token at line 70-71 is generated with `random.sample()` using Python's non-CSPRNG Mersenne Twister, and is set via a `<meta http-equiv='Set-Cookie'>` tag rather than a real `Set-Cookie` HTTP header, so no `HttpOnly` or `Secure` flags are applied and the token is accessible to JavaScript.]

HTTP Response Splitting / Header Injection via ?charset= parameter — Inject arbitrary HTTP headers; enable cache poisoning, phishing pages, or bypass security headers. [verified: `params.get('charset','utf8')` is appended to the `Content-Type` header value with no CRLF stripping, allowing header injection via `
` sequences in the charset parameter to add arbitrary headers or split the HTTP response.]

Verbose Error / Stack Trace Disclosure — Reveals server-side file paths, Python module structure, and internal application logic useful for further attacks. [verified: The exception handler at line 73-75 writes `traceback.format_exc()` directly to the HTTP response body for any unhandled exception, exposing full file paths, module names, and internal application logic to attackers.]

Security Headers Disabled / Missing — Browser XSS protections are disabled for all users; application is vulnerable to clickjacking and other client-side attacks with no mitigating browser controls. [verified: `self.send_header('X-XSS-Protection', '0')` is explicitly sent on every response, disabling the browser's built-in XSS filter; no `Content-Security-Policy`, `X-Frame-Options`, or other protective headers are set anywhere in the handler.]
